title: Neural substrates involved in the control of posture
notes: Review of neural substrates involved control posture. Automatic process of postural control, which is termed as postural reflexes including head–eye coordination accompanied by appropriate alignment of body segments, is mediated by the descending pathways from the brainstem.

title: The Effects of Spike Frequency Adaptation and Negative Feedback on the Synchronization of Neural Oscillators
notes: The two standard spike-frequency adaptation mechanisms have distinct effects on synchronization of excitatorily coupled neurons: M-current adaptation alters the mechanism of repetitive firing, whereas calcium-dependent afterhyperpolarization adaptation works by shunting incoming synapses, a mechanism that also applies in networks with recurrent inhibition. A two-variable reduced model arising near certain bifurcations and a derived one-dimensional map capture the shunting behavior.
animal_study: Pharmacologically separate the two adaptation mechanisms in coupled neural populations (selective blockers of the slow voltage-dependent potassium current versus the calcium-dependent current) and test the predicted opposite effects on synchronization.
robot_sim: Implement both adaptation types (AHP-like synaptic shunting versus M-current-like alteration of the firing mechanism) in coupled CPG oscillators and compare their effects on synchronization and burst termination.

title: Finding Resonance: Adaptive Frequency Oscillators for Dynamic Legged Locomotion
notes: Adaptive frequency oscillators automatically tune their intrinsic frequency to the resonant frequency of a compliant quadruped robot using only local sensory feedback; the learned frequency persists after the robot halts and re-adapts when body mass changes, with a linearized convergence analysis identifying which sensory feedback types support stable adaptation.
animal_study: Test whether locomotor frequency re-tunes after body-mass changes during growth in developing animals, as the adaptive-frequency account predicts from the robot's re-adaptation to mass changes.
robot_sim: Couple adaptive frequency oscillators to a compliant locomotion plant so intrinsic frequency tracks plant resonance via local feedback; verify persistence of the learned frequency at halt and re-adaptation after a mass change.

title: Deconstructing the modular organization and real-time dynamics of mammalian spinal locomotor networks
notes: In a mouse brainstem-spinal cord preparation with simultaneous Ca2+ imaging, glutamatergic neurons in the lateral paragigantocellular and caudal ventrolateral reticular nuclei directly initiate locomotion, and the descending command is executed by distinct spinal glutamatergic modules that transform it into rhythmic output, with inhibitory networks recruited in a different pattern — a modular logic for how the cord implements the locomotor command.

title: The control of foot placement during compensatory stepping reactions: does speed of response take precedence over stability?
notes: Computational model study. In this paper, a model is developed to examine how speed and stability demands affect control of foot placement during forward and backward compensatory stepping reactions.

title: Central Pattern Generator Inspired Control for Adaptive Walking of Biped Robots
notes: The proposed control strategy is able to generate adaptive joint control signals online to realize biped adaptive walking.

title: Mid-Lumbar Segments Are Needed for the Expression of Locomotion in Chronic Spinal Cats
notes: In chronically spinalized cats, a second transection at caudal L3 or L4 permanently abolishes treadmill locomotion even after weeks of training, while lesions at L2 or rostral L3 spare it; fast paw shakes and clonidine-induced hindlimb hyperextension persist below the lesion, so mid-lumbar segments are necessary specifically for locomotor rhythm expression, not for other rhythmic motor patterns or caudal motoneuron function.
animal_study: Record from L3-L4 interneuron populations during both locomotion and paw shaking, combined with the segmental transection logic, to identify which mid-lumbar circuits are locomotion-selective; test whether electrical stimulation at L3-L4 substitutes for their disconnection.
robot_sim: Model a spatially distributed spinal network where only mid-lumbar-equivalent modules generate the locomotor pattern while caudal segments retain reflex and rhythmic capacity; ablating the mid-lumbar module should eliminate gait but leave paw-shake-like rhythmicity intact.

title: Human hip–ankle coordination emerging from multisensory feedback control
notes: Computational model study. This study postu- lates that the coordination emerges from interactions on the sen- sory levels in the feedback control.

title: Exercise, music, and the brain: Is there a central pattern generator?
notes: Vertical body oscillation during self-paced running clusters at 2.7-2.8 Hz, matching dominant frequencies of heart rate and of runners' preferred music, with EEG delta power rising after running — supporting the speculation that a common ~3 Hz oscillator, possibly a locomotor central pattern generator, couples intrinsic and extrinsic rhythms during exercise.
animal_study: Record locomotor, autonomic, and cortical rhythms concurrently in running animals before and after spinal transection to test whether the ~3 Hz coupling survives spinalization, which would localize the shared oscillator to a spinal CPG as speculated.
robot_sim: Embed a CPG in a neuromechanical running model driving coupled oscillator loads representing autonomic and cortical-like subsystems, and test frequency locking to the locomotor rhythm under speed changes.

title: Stability Analysis of Legged Locomotion Models by Symmetry-Factored Return Maps
notes: Symmetry-factored return maps yield an exact algebraic necessary condition for asymptotic stability (and a sufficient condition for instability) of fixed points in 2DoF and 3DoF spring-loaded inverted pendulum models, despite the non-integrability of the SLIP dynamics. The expression characterizes analytically the sensory cost and stabilizing benefit of feedback schemes previously proposed for the 2DoF SLIP model of running and extends to a 3DoF descriptive model of the robot RHex.
robot_sim: Apply the symmetry-factored return-map analysis to a hybrid legged model's dynamics to rank candidate feedback schemes by stabilizing benefit per sensory cost before implementing any of them in a controller.

title: Synaptic control of hindlimb motoneurones during three forms of the fictive scratch reflex in the turtle.
notes: Intracellular recordings for three distinct forms of turtle scratch reflex in response to tactile stimulation of body surface.

title: The role of Renshaw cells in locomotion: antagonism of their excitation from motor axon collaterals with intravenous mecamylamine
notes: Blocking nicotinic transmission from motor axon collaterals with mecamylamine during fictive locomotion abolished recurrent IPSPs and rhythmic Renshaw firing yet left locomotor drive potentials, burst timing, and Ia inhibitory interneuron rhythmicity intact, with motoneuron and Ia-inhibitory-interneuron bursts carrying more spikes at higher frequency - establishing that Renshaw cells are not part of the locomotor CPG and do not time bursts, but limit firing rates within them.
animal_study: Chronically silence Renshaw cells (nicotinic antagonists or chemogenetics) during locomotion and compare motoneuron and Ia inhibitory interneuron firing-rate distributions to test the rate-limiting role without rhythm effects.
robot_sim: Implement Renshaw cells as recurrent negative feedback acting only on motoneuron and Ia-inhibitory-interneuron firing rates; ablating them in simulation should raise within-burst firing while leaving burst timing and the locomotor rhythm unchanged.

title: A model of spindle afferent response to muscle stretch
notes: Computational model study. A unified model of the properties of stretch responses of mammalian spindle end- ings is proposed.

title: Functional organization within the medullary reticular formation of the intact unanesthetized cat. III. Microstimulation during locomotion.
notes: Microstimulation of the cat medullary reticular formation during locomotion evokes phase-dependent responses incorporated into the ongoing pattern — flexor excitation in each limb during that muscle's natural activity period, inhibition of ipsilateral extensors, mixed responses in contralateral vastus lateralis — with response latencies shortest during a muscle's active period, showing that reticulospinal transmission is gated by the locomotor network itself.
animal_study: Repeat the stimulation protocol in deafferented or fictively locomoting preparations to determine how much of the phase-dependent gating of reticulospinal effects is produced centrally by the locomotor network versus by phasic sensory feedback.
robot_sim: Implement descending reticulospinal-like drive onto a CPG with phase-dependent pathway gating (gain high during each muscle's active phase) and reproduce the shortening of response latency with activity state as a test of state-dependent transmission.

title: Distribution of Heterogenic Reflexes Among the Quadriceps and Triceps Surae Muscles of the Cat Hind Limb
notes: Heterogenic proprioceptive reflexes among cat quadriceps and triceps surae are organized by articulation rather than motor-unit composition: excitatory length feedback strongly links the uniarticular vastus muscles (and vastus to soleus) to regulate joint stiffness, while force-related inhibition is absent between vastus muscles but strong and bidirectional between vastus and rectus femoris and between triceps surae and quadriceps - regulating interjoint coupling and, together with length feedback, the endpoint mechanical properties.
animal_study: Selective tendon-organ or spindle inactivation during controlled stretches of the same muscle set would dissociate the length and force components of the articulation-based organization.
robot_sim: Implement heterogenic feedback by articulation: excitatory length feedback among uniarticular synergists for joint stiffness, bidirectional force inhibition between muscles spanning different joints for interjoint coupling; ablate the interjoint force inhibition to test endpoint property regulation.

title: Sensory Feedback Mechanism Underlying Entrainment of Central Pattern Generator to Mechanical Resonance
notes: Identifies the neuronal properties required for a CPG to entrain to mechanical resonance: comparing reciprocal-inhibition oscillator models coupled to a pendulum, robust entrainment arises from strong positive-feedback coupling to the lightly damped mechanics when the neurons possess complete adaptation - established by comparative numerical experiments and harmonic-balance analysis of the minimal model.
animal_study: Load or stiffen a limb in a walking animal and test whether locomotor frequency tracks the shifted mechanical resonance - the model's hallmark prediction of sensory-feedback-mediated entrainment.
robot_sim: Implement a reciprocal-inhibition oscillator CPG with adapting neurons strongly and positively coupled to a lightly damped limb; ablate neuronal adaptation to demonstrate loss of resonance entrainment - a direct recipe for neuromechanical frequency locking.

title: Tetraspine: Robust terrain handling on a tensegrity robot using central pattern generators
notes: Computational model study. —In order to produce a new mode of robust robotic locomotion and better understand how vertebrates coordinate motion with a compliant spine, we are developing a modular tensegrity robot inspired by the spine.

title: Sensory feedback plays a significant role in generating walking gait and in gait transition in salamanders: a simulation study
notes: A 3D neuro-musculo-mechanical salamander model shows proprioceptive feedback - girdle stretch-receptor-like intraspinal neurons plus hip and scapula limb stretch receptors - is essential for a coordinated lateral-sequence walking gait, while walking trot is dominated by the CPG; the walk-to-trot transition can be induced by increased descending drive from the mesencephalic locomotor region and is helped by hip/scapula sensory input signaling late stance. Demonstrates that the sensory-versus-central balance of control differs by gait.
animal_study: The authors' own call: identify the mechanoreceptor types and modulation mechanisms in the salamander girdles and limbs electrophysiologically, and test the gait-transition prediction by stimulating the mesencephalic locomotor region while selectively blocking hip/scapula stretch-receptor input.
robot_sim: Implement girdle and hip/scapula stretch-receptor feedback onto a body-CPG plus four limb-CPGs network in simulation; ablate the sensory modulation to check that lateral-sequence walking degrades while trot survives, and gate the walk-to-trot switch on late-stance stretch detection with increasing descending drive.

title: Spinal cords: Symphonies of interneurons across species
notes: Review of spinal interneuron composition across vertebrates: fish run on two basic classes (ipsilateral excitatory and commissural inhibitory neurons) plus ipsilateral inhibition for escape swimming, and with the evolution of limbs these three types proliferated into molecularly, anatomically, and functionally distinct subpopulations — movement elaboration is mirrored by interneuron specialization.

title: The Ia afferent feedback of a given movement evokes the illusion of the same movement when returned to the subject via muscle tendon vibration
notes: The results show that the Ia aﬀerent feedback of a given movement evokes the illu- sion of the same movement when it is applied to the subject via the appropriate pattern of muscle tendon vibration.

title: Phase-dependent modulation of primary afferent depolarization in single cutaneous primary afferents evoked by peripheral stimulation during fictive locomotion in the cat
notes: Cutaneous primary afferent terminals in the cat hindlimb are rhythmically depolarized during fictive locomotion (L-PAD), and primary afferent depolarization evoked by peripheral nerve stimulation is phase-modulated by the CPG - minimal during flexion, maximal during extension - so presynaptic inhibitory gating of cutaneous reflex transmission is locomotor-phase dependent. Centrally generated and peripherally evoked presynaptic mechanisms are in part separately controlled, since evoked PAD peaked in extension regardless of L-PAD amplitude.
animal_study: Record intra-axonally from identified cutaneous afferents during real (non-fictive) locomotion to test the prediction that movement-related presynaptic inhibition is phase-modulated, or pharmacologically block GABAergic PAD to test the consequences for phase-dependent cutaneous reflex gating.
robot_sim: Implement locomotor-phase-dependent presynaptic gain on cutaneous feedback channels (lowest during flexion, highest during extension) in a reflex-gated walker, then ablate the gating to quantify its contribution to reflex timing and gait stability.

title: Bioinspired morphing wings for extended flight envelope and roll control of small drones
notes: We show that a fully deployed configuration enhances manoeuvrability while a folded configuration offers low drag at high speeds and is beneficial in strong headwinds.

title: The effects of self-reinnervation of cat medial and lateral gastrocnemius muscles on hindlimb kinematics in slope walking
notes: Self-reinnervation of cat gastrocnemius muscles (motor function recovers, proprioceptive feedback permanently absent) leaves level- and upslope-walking kinematics recovered within 14-19 weeks but produces permanent ankle and interjoint deficits in downslope walking - indicating MG/LG proprioceptive feedback is specifically required for regulating ankle extensors on downslope, with compensation by other sensory sources (e.g., cutaneous) or altered central drive elsewhere.
animal_study: Combine MG/LG self-reinnervation with graded cutaneous anesthesia during downslope walking to test whether cutaneous input is the compensating sensory source for the lost muscle proprioception.
robot_sim: Ablate length and force feedback from ankle extensors in a slope-walking simulator: level and upslope gaits should tolerate the loss via central-drive/cutaneous compensation while downslope develops persistent ankle yield - a test of feedback redundancy.

title: Primacy of Flexor Locomotor Pattern Revealed by Ancestral Reversion of Motor Neuron Identity
notes: Ancestral reversion of lumbar motor neuron identity reveals the primacy of the flexor locomotor pattern; flexor-dominant circuitry appears to be the conserved building block of limb locomotion.

title: The pyloric central pattern generator in Crustacea: a set of conditional neuronal oscillators
notes: This was shown by isolating in situ pyloric neurons from all other elements in the pyloric network.

title: Nature of Motor Control: Perspectives and Issues
notes: Computational model study. Four perspectives on motor control provide the framework for developing a comprehensive theory of motor control in biological systems.

title: Multi-expert learning of adaptive legged locomotion
notes: A multi-expert learning architecture gates and blends pretrained deep-network experts and synthesizes new policies online, letting a single quadruped controller trot, steer, and recover from falls on real hardware — a machine-learning route to the adaptive multiskill locomotion that fixed CPG controllers lack.

title: How Do We Approach the Locomotor Network in the Mammalian Spinal Cord?a
notes: Critical essay on strategies for delineating the mammalian locomotor network; questions the rhythm-center consensus and outlines testable network approaches.

title: Postural Compensation for Unilateral Vestibular Loss
notes: Computational model study. Results showed that UVL subjects made signiﬁcantly greater use of proprioceptive, and therefore less use of vestibular, orientation information on all tests.

title: Diversity of molecularly defined spinal interneurons engaged in mammalian locomotor pattern generation.
notes: Review of the four cardinal classes of molecularly defined ventral spinal interneurons (from ten progenitor domains) and their contribution to mammalian locomotor pattern generation, organizing each population by excitatory versus inhibitory action and axonal projection as candidate rhythm-generating versus coordinating elements.

title: Intra-muscle Synergies Stabilizing Reflex-mediated Force Changes
notes:
Highlights
•
Reflex-mediated finger force changes are stabilized by intra-muscle synergies.

•
No synergies in the space of individual finger force stabilized the force changes.

•
Effects of dominance are seen in inter-finger but not intra-muscle synergies.

•
Effects of motor equivalence are seen during reflex-induced force changes.


Abstract
We used the framework of the uncontrolled manifold hypothesis to explore force-stabilizing synergies and motor equivalence in the spaces of individual motor unit (MU) firing frequencies. Healthy subjects performed steady force production tasks by pressing with one finger or three fingers of a hand. Surface EMG was used to identify individual MU action potentials. MUs formed stable groups (MU-modes) with parallel scaling of the firing frequency in both flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) and extensor digitorum communis (EDC) that allowed identifying them with the reciprocal and coactivation commands. Smooth lifting of the fingers by an “inverse piano” device led to an unintentional, reflex-based force increase. There was significantly larger motion in the space of MU-modes that kept the force unchanged (motor equivalent) compared to motion that changed force (non-motor equivalent). The force change was stabilized by co-varying contributions of the MU-modes defined separately for FDS and EDC. title: Central pattern generators for bipedal locomotion
notes: We show that breaking the symmetry between fore and hind limbs in quad, which yields the CPGarm, leads to periodic solution types whose associated leg rhythms correspond to seven of the eight leg gaits found in leg; the missing biped gait is the asymmetric hop.

title: Review and perspective: neuromechanical considerations for predicting muscle activation patterns for movement
notes: Review of review perspective: neuromechanical considerations predicting muscle. Computational model study. In postural control, we demonstrate that temporal patterns of muscle activity may be governed by feedback control of task-level variables that represent the overall goal-directed motion of the body.

title: Performance of a model for a local neuron population
notes: A three-subset local neuron population model — main and auxiliary excitatory subsets plus an inhibitory subset, wired in positive and negative feedback loops — produces rhythmic activity under white-noise input in its stable regime and input-dependent limit cycles at higher mean input, with an electronic realization generating EEG-like background activity and paroxysmal spikes.
robot_sim: Use the excitatory-inhibitory population loop architecture as a building block when adding inhibitory subsets to CPG layers, sweeping input level to map stable rhythmic output versus limit-cycle regimes.

title: Motoneuronal and muscle synergies involved in cat hindlimb control during fictive and real locomotion: a comparison study
notes: Markin and Rybak model. Cat EMG data. Focus on synergies.

title: Secondary endings of muscle spindles: Structure, reflex action, role in motor control and proprioception
notes: Review of secondary endings muscle spindles: structure, reflex action,. There are two types of sensory endings, primary and secondary, with differing development, morphology, distribution and responsiveness.

title: Influence of Stance Width on Frontal Plane Postural Dynamics and Coordination in Human Balance Control
notes: Results show that the narrow stance postural system is nonlinear across stimulus ampli- tude in both EO and EC conditions, whereas the wide stance postural system is more linear.

title: On the definition of central pattern generator and its sensory control
notes: Computational model study. For the intact animal, model considerations show that this term is neither clearly delimited from the concept of a reflex chain nor from the concept of a pattern generator with functional principles different from those of the CPG.

title: Spinal interneurons providing input to the final common path during locomotion
notes: Spinal interneurons providing input to the final common path during locomotion; framework relating interneuron diversity to the assembly of locomotor commands.

title: Could Different Directions of Infant Stepping Be Controlled by the Same Locomotor Central Pattern Generator?
notes: Human infants who sustain forward stepping can also step sideways and backward on a treadmill, with the same relationships of stance and swing phase durations to cycle duration across directions and speeds, and no discrete changes in electromyographic or temporal parameters when direction is varied continuously, supporting a single locomotor CPG controlling different walking directions with direction-specific muscle tuning (for example hamstrings much more active in backward swing).
animal_study: In animal models, rotate the walking direction gradually on a treadmill while recording limb kinematics and EMG, testing for continuous retuning rather than discrete pattern switching as evidence for a shared CPG.
robot_sim: Drive a single locomotor CPG through a direction-dependent motoneuron mapping and test continuous direction changes for graded, EMG-like retuning without discrete pattern switches.

title: Fixed-wing MAV attitude stability in atmospheric turbulence—Part 2: Investigating biologically-inspired sensors
notes: Bio-inspired ﬂow and pressure-based sensors were found to be the most promising for complementing or replacing current inertial-based reactive attitude sensors.

title: Adaptation of postural control to perturbations—a process that initiates long-term motor memory
notes: The ﬁndings suggest that balance rehabilitation should include a variety of repeated exercises, which are sufﬁciently long to induce habituation.

title: Initiating or Blocking Locomotion in Spinal Cats by Applying Noradrenergic Drugs to Restricted Lumbar Spinal Segments
notes: Focal alpha2-noradrenergic action at restricted lumbar levels both starts and stops spinal walking: topical clonidine over L3-L4 or L5-L7, or microinjection at L3-L5, induces treadmill locomotion in acutely spinalized cats, whereas yohimbine at L3-L5 (not L6) or a transection at L3-L4 blocks it — mid-lumbar segments are a sufficient pharmacological trigger and a necessary substrate for the rhythm.
animal_study: Combine segment-restricted clonidine/yohimbine application with selective deafferentation or graded sensory perturbations to test how mid-lumbar rhythmogenesis interacts with afferent gating; alternatively test in chronic preparations whether repeated L3-L4 noradrenergic stimulation enhances recovery of stepping.
robot_sim: Build a spatially segmented spinal CPG in which only mid-lumbar-equivalent modules can be tonically activated to launch the full hindlimb pattern; ablating those modules while leaving caudal motoneuron pools functional should abolish gait but spare other rhythmic outputs.

title: Analysis of Chaotic Resonance in Izhikevich Neuron Model
notes: Classifies the chaotic regimes of the Izhikevich neuron model - a primarily turbulent state and an intermittent chaotic state - using Lyapunov exponents with a saltation matrix and Poincare sections, then shows both exhibit chaotic resonance: sensitive response to weak sub-threshold periodic signals without noise, with the intermittent state responding more promptly.
robot_sim: Operate Izhikevich CPG units in intermittent-chaos parameter regimes to exploit chaotic resonance for detecting weak periodic sensory signals, comparing detection latency against stochastic-resonance noise injection.

title: Emulating Balance Control Observed in Human Test Subjects with a Neural Network
Multifrequency Hebbian plasticity in coupled neural oscillators
notes: Analyzes Hebbian plasticity in weakly connected oscillator networks with frequency detuning (gradient-frequency neural networks): learning produces stronger connections for simple frequency ratios than for complex ones, and the plasticity is locally dominated by a nonlinear resonance captured by the two-frequency model — a candidate self-organizing mechanism for intersegmental coordination.
animal_study: Test the ratio-dependence in vitro: co-activate two coupled neuronal oscillators with distinct intrinsic frequencies (e.g., spinal hemicord pairs) and assay coupling-strength changes for simple versus complex frequency ratios as the Hebbian model predicts.
robot_sim: Add a Hebbian update rule to connections between frequency-detuned CPG oscillators; verify simple-ratio couplings strengthen preferentially, then ablate learning and measure coordination loss.

title: NEURAL NETWORK DYNAMICS
notes: Review of neural network dynamics. Computational model study. We also review propagation of stimulus-driven activity through sponta- neously active networks.

title: Model Predictive Control for Gust Load Alleviation
notes: Computational model study. The proposed controller design takes actuator deﬂection- and rate-limitations, the complex multiple- inputs multiple-outputs system structure, and the objective to reduce critical loads directly into account.

title: Attitude and Altitude Controller Design for Quad-Rotor Type MAVs
notes: Computational model study. In order to show the effectiveness of the PD-A over the PD, theoretical and experimental studies were carried out based on one degree of freedom quadcopter model.

title: Observers for Canonic Models of Neural Oscillators
notes: Observer-design analysis of canonic neural oscillator models (Hodgkin-Huxley, Hindmarsh-Rose, FitzHugh-Nagumo, Morris-Lecar): they are locally observable but not in adaptive observer canonic form, and no parameter-independent diffeomorphism converts them; parameter-dependent transformations nevertheless allow partial state/parameter reconstruction with exponential convergence, and a Lyapunov plus positive-invariance/small-gain method handles nonlinearly entering parameters while avoiding ill-conditioning and non-uniqueness.
robot_sim: Apply these observers to estimate hidden states and parameters of neural oscillator/CPG models in real time from sparse outputs (a few state components plus the input signal), enabling online identification and tuning of simulated CPGs and model-based decoding for closed-loop neural control.

title: Cutaneous inputs from perineal region facilitates and modulates spinal locomotor activity and reduces cutaneous reflexes from the foot in spinal cats
notes: In spinal cats, mechanical stimulation of the perineal region triggers and re-times rhythmic locomotor activity — shortening cycle and burst durations and increasing flexor and extensor burst amplitudes — while simultaneously decreasing short-latency ipsilateral and contralateral cutaneous reflexes from the foot across joints and limbs. The locomotor facilitation therefore reflects excitation of CPG circuitry with state-dependent reflex suppression by spinal interneurons, not an increase in cutaneous reflex gain.
animal_study: In spinal cats, record CPG interneurons during perineal stimulation to test whether the excitation lands directly on rhythm circuitry, and selectively anesthetize perineal skin or section the relevant dorsal roots to confirm the afferent origin of both the facilitation and the reflex suppression.
robot_sim: Implement a tonic cutaneous (perineal-analog) input that raises CPG drive while scaling down short-latency reflex gains; the model should show shorter cycles, larger bursts, and reduced cutaneous reflex responses, testing state-dependent reflex gating layered on a CPG.

title: Neuronal specification in the spinal cord: inductive signals and transcriptional codes
notes: Reviews the developmental logic of spinal neuronal specification: inductive signals and transcriptional codes assign class identity to progenitors at defined positions in the neural tube, assembling neural circuits with the selective connectivity that underlies the mature organism's behavioral repertoire.
animal_study: Misexpress or knock down the inductive signals and transcriptional codes in the developing neural tube and assay whether the predicted interneuron classes fail to differentiate and whether circuit connectivity and behavior change accordingly.

title: Dynamical Systems in Neuroscience: The Geometry of Excitability and Bursting
notes: Standard reference connecting electrophysiology to nonlinear dynamical systems theory: neuronal information processing depends on dynamical as well as electrophysiological properties, with excitability, bursting, and synchronization treated geometrically (phase planes, bifurcations) starting from one- and two-dimensional Hodgkin-Huxley-type models. Provides the analysis toolkit for classifying the operating regime and burst-termination mechanisms of CPG neuron models.
robot_sim: Use its phase-plane and bifurcation methods to classify the operating regime and burst-termination mechanism of CPG half-center and persistent-sodium neuron models before porting them across simulators, where bifurcation regime — not parameter identity — determines transfer.

title: Neuronal Control of LocomotionFrom Mollusc to Man
notes: Comparative monograph surveying the neural mechanisms of locomotion across evolutionarily diverse species, from leech swimming to human running, synthesizing CPG organization, descending control, and sensory regulation into unifying principles of how nervous systems generate locomotion; a canonical cross-species reference for locomotor neurobiology.
robot_sim: Use its comparative survey of CPG organization and descending control across species to select conserved motifs (half-center rhythm cores, brainstem initiation and speed control) as architecture choices for robotic locomotor controllers.

title: The Circuitry of the Human Spinal Cord: Its Role in Motor Control and Movement Disorders
notes: Reference monograph on human spinal circuitry — descending tracts, reflex pathways, and their pathophysiology in movement disorders.

title: Neuromechanical Modeling of Posture and Locomotion
notes: Book

title: Modeling the Organization of Spinal Cord Neural Circuits Controlling Two-Joint Muscles
notes: Chapter of the Neuromechanical Modeling of Posture and Locomotion book.

title: Effects of muscle dynamics and proprioceptive feedback on the kinematics and CPG activity of salamander stepping
notes: Conference abstract: in an 8-joint salamander stepping model without feedback, trunk kinematics deviate from the EMG pattern, illustrating the effect of muscle dynamics (motion closer to a standing wave), and feedback in a 10-joint model modulates CPG activity.
robot_sim: Reproduce salamander stepping models with and without muscle dynamics and with CPG feedback modulation (8- versus 10-joint versions), quantifying how muscle dynamics decouple trunk kinematics from the EMG pattern and how feedback modulates the CPG.
